content.text:
**Observations:**
- **Initialisation scale.** Most first-layer weights sit in about ±0.035, roughly 1/√784. That is the untouched initialisation range, so pixels with weights this small were rarely non-zero during training.
- **Image corners.** The first few pixels of row 0 (inputs 0–5) and the last pixels of row 27 stay at that small scale. The corners were almost always black.
- **Top row.** The middle of row 0 has clearly trained weights. Inputs 10–17 reach |w| ≈ 0.2–0.29. Row 1 behaves the same way (inputs 38–39 and 45–46 reach about 0.3–0.42).
- **Bottom row.** The middle of row 27 also has large weights, about ±0.25 at inputs ~768–769.
- **Side columns.** There is a strongly periodic pattern with period 28: one line per image row. These lines sit at the right edge of each row (inputs 27, 55, 83, …) and at the column just before it. They carry large weights, e.g. −0.19 to −0.22 on unit 2, −0.18 to −0.25 on unit 11, −0.14 to −0.17 on unit 15 and +0.15 on unit 6. The left-edge columns are also active. So pixels at the image borders, over most of the image height, were often bright.
- **Hidden units.** The units look like broad, blob-like silhouette detectors rather than thin stroke detectors. They respond to "wide object touching the left and right edges", "object reaching the top or bottom" and centre-versus-periphery contrasts.
- **Output layer.** Each class draws on a mix of these silhouette units with weights up to about ±1.5, and no single unit is dedicated to one class.

**Reasoning:**
- **MNIST-style digit sets are unlikely.** In MNIST (and EMNIST/KMNIST, which share its 20×20-box-in-28×28 centring), the outer rows and columns are almost always zero. Weights there would stay at their initial values. Here the top row, bottom row and side columns all carry some of the largest weights in the network.
- **Clothing silhouettes fit well.** Fashion-MNIST objects are scaled to fill the frame:
  - Shirts, pullovers and coats span the full width, which explains the active left and right columns across many rows.
  - Trousers, dresses and ankle boots reach the bottom row.
  - Bag handles and shirt collars reach the top row.
  - The corners still stay mostly empty, which matches what is seen.
- **Broad detectors fit too.** Blob-like, region-level hidden units suit coarse shape discrimination such as wide versus narrow or tall versus short. They do not look like the thin stroke detectors a digit classifier would need.

**Dataset:** Fashion-MNIST (Zalando's 28×28 grayscale product images).

**Classes:** 0 T-shirt/top, 1 Trouser, 2 Pullover, 3 Dress, 4 Coat, 5 Sandal, 6 Shirt, 7 Sneaker, 8 Bag, 9 Ankle boot.

**Confidence:** 72%
